title: Fonio with Grilled Lamb Chops, Asparagus and Mafé Sauce
localName: Fonio, côtelettes d’agneau et sauce mafé
author: Pierre Thiam
desc: Thyme-and-garlic lamb chops grilled about five minutes a side, asparagus charred three, fonio steamed and a sauce of two cups of peanut butter in a quart of chicken broth.
longDesc: A restaurant plate. The mafé sauce comes first: onion cooks 3 to 5 minutes until soft but not brown, a tablespoon of tomato paste cooks about 5 minutes on low, then two cups of smooth peanut butter and a quart of chicken broth, with a whole Scotch bonnet if wanted, simmer 15 to 20 minutes until oil rises to the surface. Eight chops are rubbed with oil, thyme, garlic, salt and pepper and grilled about 5 minutes a side, rested 5 minutes under foil; asparagus grills about 3 minutes. Fonio is cooked on the stovetop in about 5 minutes covered plus 2 more off the heat, or microwaved 6–8 minutes.
ingredients: 8 lamb chops, trimmed of excess fat
1 cup raw fonio, rinsed and drained well
1 tbsp peanut, vegetable or olive oil (optional)
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high. Cook the onion 3 to 5 minutes, until soft but not brown. Add the tomato paste, reduce to low and stir about 5 minutes, until deep red. Add a few tablespoons of water only if needed to prevent scorching.

Stir in the peanut butter, then the chicken broth. Bring to a boil, add the Scotch bonnet if using, reduce to a simmer and cook, stirring periodically, 15 to 20 minutes, until the oil rises to the surface. Remove from the heat and keep warm.
Heat a grill to high. Rub the chops with the oil, thyme, garlic, 1 teaspoon salt and the pepper. Grill about 5 minutes per side, until nicely browned and medium (adjust for thickness).
Transfer the chops to a platter, cover loosely with foil and rest 5 minutes.
While the lamb rests, season the asparagus with salt and grill about 3 minutes, turning occasionally, until nicely charred.

Fonio: boil the water and salt, add the fonio, stir once, reduce to a simmer, cover tightly and cook about 5 minutes. Turn off the heat and keep covered 2 more minutes, until the water is absorbed. Fluff and mix in the oil if using.
Serve the lamb and fonio with a generous amount of sauce.
chefTips: ‘Until the oil rises to the surface’ is the sauce cue.
The peanut-to-liquid ratio here (2 cups butter to 1 quart broth) is far thicker than the shank mafé (1 cup to 2 quarts): it is a sauce, not a stew.
Rest the chops under foil for 5 minutes before slicing into them.
Fonio microwave option: 1 cup fonio, 2 cups water, 1 tsp salt, covered tightly with plastic, high 6–8 minutes.
storage: The sauce 4 days refrigerated; the lamb best fresh.
reheating: Sauce gently with a splash of broth.
healthBenefits: Lamb supplies iron and zinc; asparagus adds folate.
culturalNote: The page does not say the recipe comes from ‘The Fonio Cookbook’ — it links that book only as a related title — so it is catalogued as unattributed to a specific book. The date is not printed on the page; the URL indicates 28 August 2020.

Book source NOT STATED. Yield not stated for the main recipe; the fonio sub-recipes each make 3 to 4 cups (4 used here). SINGLE-PASS.

PRINTED RATIO flagged: 2 cups unsweetened smooth peanut butter against 1 quart chicken broth is a far higher peanut-to-liquid ratio than the Lake Isle shank mafé (1 cup to 2 quarts). Reported as printed; not reconciled.
Salt has no quantity in the ingredient list; the method calls for 1 teaspoon on the chops.

Cues in short fragments: onion ‘soft but not brown’; paste ‘until deep red’; sauce ‘until oil rises to the surface’; chops ‘nicely browned and medium’; asparagus ‘nicely charred’; fonio ‘until the water is absorbed’. No oven temperatures — heat only high, medium-high, low and simmer.
